data.content: # Braves predicted to sign ex-Mets $38M veteran two-time all-Star to bolster rotation with Chris Sale. For the Atlanta Braves, the 2026 season was full of ups and downs as the team won the NL East once again. It wasn't easy, and injuries to the starting rotation played a big part in making the season difficult. The rotation is an area where the Braves have struggled over the years, and it is something they just can't seem to shake. As the team heads down the stretch, there’s now even more scrutiny on a few things: the lack of a potent 1-2 punch for the postseason, their bullpen's durability and the rotation's overall dependability,” MLB.com’s Jason Foster wrote. With the 2027 season approaching, it is unclear what Atlanta's starting rotation will look like. “While it wasn’t their downfall in the end, the starting rotation has been a constant thorn in the Atlanta Braves’ side for multiple seasons now.
